evals.prompt: Be my shepherd. I'm in Herdr but there's no .shepherd/instructions.md here. Which agents need my attention in this session?
evals.expected_output: Work one-off without creating files; discover recognized agents first, exclude self, inspect relevant evidence, distinguish idle/done/blocked, and report actionable items only for the inherited session as a numbered list, not a table. Each item puts the live pane/workspace locator in its heading, followed by subject-level Context, Status, Needs, Next. Explain the actual change and user workflow without requiring a link click; status-only issue numbers/test counts do not satisfy Context. Check navigation availability and offer missing setup without blocking the brief; summarize other agents briefly.

evals.prompt: The babyclaw workspace has three empty panes after a restart. Find the agent work we might have left behind.
evals.expected_output: Check shell process state and local agent-history for the cwd, distinguish saved sessions from live agents, avoid assigning a historical session to a pane without evidence, and do not resume or type into shells without authorization.

evals.prompt: Push the idle agent in workspace w5 forward on the issue it just said was ready for implementation. Don't do its work for it.
evals.expected_output: Refresh agent identity, foreground output and dirty repo state; send a bounded continuation prompt to the existing owner only, inspect delivery and progress, never blindly retry a timed-out send, and don't implement, approve, commit or push on its behalf.

evals.prompt: Set up this directory for a recurring Shepherd for workday coordination. Keep my standing scope and reporting preferences here, but don't copy my task backlog.
evals.expected_output: Inspect existing files and project conventions; create .shepherd/instructions.md only for this explicit setup request, holding standing scope and preferences without transcripts, secrets, statuses or a copied backlog. Explain remembering work in plain language, confirm the directory/remit and saved data, then use scoped atomic helper writes rather than storing status in instructions. Do not crawl agents during setup or launch a summary after it; offer to check agents next and wait.

evals.prompt: I'm already in a Herdr session. Take a look at my other named Herdr session too and nudge any idle agents over there.
evals.expected_output: State that this Shepherd is bound to the inherited session, do not attach to or target another session, and suggest starting a separate Shepherd there; don't nudge agents outside scope.

evals.prompt: Give me a short first brief. I don't remember what each agent was working on. Link me directly to panes that need pushing if possible, but this Herdr installation has no verified pane URL.
evals.expected_output: Show Shepherd's local version and use numbered attention items, not a table; each item has a descriptive subject and live location, then Context, Status, Needs, Next. Context explains what behavior the work changes; tests/implementation progress go in Status. Check navigation registration, offer setup if missing, and while awaiting approval keep the meaningful pane name/title (or ID fallback) plain with a focus command rather than fabricate a URL. Link actual work records separately. Do not focus or open candidate links during read-only triage.

evals.prompt: Give me a short attention brief. This Herdr host has documented links to live panes and workspaces, and their exact destinations can be verified from metadata without opening them.
evals.expected_output: Use a numbered list with subject-level Context, Status, Needs, Next. Put the generated verified destination on the meaningful live pane name/title, falling back to ID; use workspace name with ID fallback for workspace-only destinations. Disambiguate duplicate names with pane ID, without a Go to field. Verify shepherd-navigation registration before using its URL generator; link canonical issue/PR/doc records separately. Don't invent a URI, open candidate links, or change focus during triage.

evals.prompt: Give me one brief for two agents: one has a verified pane link and the other has only a live pane ID and an issue URL. Help me reach each without moving my view now.
evals.expected_output: Use numbered items, not table rows. Use a working pane link only for the first agent; for the second, show its workspace/pane ID and copyable focus command plus a separate issue link. Briefly explain each agent's task before its blocker. Don't apply one navigation method to all items or focus either pane during the brief.

evals.prompt: Thanks for the Shepherd brief. Push item 2 forward, please; the pane list may have changed since you wrote it.
evals.expected_output: Resolve item 2 against the numbered brief as a temporary reference, refresh the live agent and pane identity before dispatch, ask if the mapping is ambiguous, and never treat the ordinal as a persistent ID or prompt a different pane occupant.

evals.prompt: Recover this configured Shepherd after a crash. threads.json has one active thread whose next step says a continuation prompt was about to be sent; its old pane is now empty. It also has one parked thread.
evals.expected_output: Derive inherited scope independently and reconcile checkpoint pointers with current-session live state and local history. Explain uncertain prompt delivery; no automatic resend, historical-session restore, outside-session search, or deletion on missing pane. Keep parked work parked and ask about unresolved recovery. Preserve malformed/schema-mismatched files and block failed checkpoints before dispatch.

evals.prompt: Park the tracked parser review for later, then remove the tracked test thread that I am explicitly wrapping up. Don't close agents or alter the issues.
evals.expected_output: Keep the parser thread with state parked and minimal recovery pointers via the scoped atomic helper. Remove the wrapped test thread, not a tombstone or wrapped history entry. No agent close, external status mutation, or deletion of underlying work. On later resume, retain its active checkpoint until explicitly wrapped/discarded.

evals.prompt: Be my Shepherd. The existing checkpoint says I last used a different skill version. Also enable clickable pane IDs here; I approve the bundled navigation plugin setup.
evals.expected_output: Report the local metadata version, read its bundled changelog, summarize relevant changes and update last_seen_skill_version only in an existing matching checkpoint. With approved navigation setup, review and link the installed navigation directory and verify registration only. Do not inventory agents or generate live pane links without a requested brief or target; offer to check agents and wait. No OS scheme registration or unsolicited focus. A one-off invocation without checkpoints would not create state merely to remember a version.

evals.prompt: I forgot what this pane is about. Its latest output only says issue #42 is implemented locally, 206 tests passed, and independent QA and mobile checks remain. Earlier local context establishes that it changes export jobs to survive interrupted browser connections. Give me a brief I can understand without opening the pane or issue.
evals.expected_output: Use a subject-level label and Context explaining resumable export jobs and interrupted connections, based on the supplied earlier evidence. Put owner-reported implementation/test results in Status, remaining checks in Needs and a concrete owner-directed verification in Next. Do not describe issue #42 or its test count as the context, invent unobserved QA details, or imply independent verification. If earlier evidence were unavailable, state the subject is unknown and inspect further or clarify rather than fabricate it.

evals.prompt: Help me enable clickable agent names in Shepherd. Your skill is installed but the navigation plugin is absent; explain and ask before installing. I have not asked for a brief or picked a target agent.
evals.expected_output: Check registration and explain the handler bridges Ctrl-click to validated focus; a skill install alone does not register it. Explain the click-to-jump option plainly and offer once to enable it, waiting for approval or explicit standing authorization. This navigation setup request does not authorize a herd-wide brief; do not crawl unrelated agents. Do not silently link, focus, register an OS scheme, repeatedly ask after refusal, or claim links work. If approved, link the installed path and verify enabled registration/root/manifest/action only; surface any exact setup blocker. Wait for a requested brief or target before generating live URLs.

evals.prompt: You're the Shepherd of this herd.
evals.expected_output: Perform lightweight Herdr-access, local-setup/version and navigation-registration checks only. Go directly to the short two-choice plain-language welcome: check on agents now, or set things up to pick up where the user left off next time. A harness-required neutral pre-load progress line is acceptable only if it says it will load guidance/check local setup and wait; it must not promise a herd scan. The welcome is the first substantive answer and then it waits. Stop and wait. Do not list agents/workspaces/panes, read transcripts, search history, inspect canonical work, reconcile threads, or create setup. Avoid continuity/checkpoint/handler/config-filename jargon in the welcome.

evals.prompt: Be my Shepherd. This directory already has standing instructions and several saved active and parked threads, but I haven't asked you to review them yet.
evals.expected_output: Existing setup does not authorize a herd crawl or checkpoint reconciliation. Run only lightweight activation checks, use the returning-user welcome: say setup was found and offer to check agents now or change setup. Stop for the choice. Do not list thread titles, resume work, or update thread state.

evals.prompt: Be my Shepherd. I already set this up last week. The saved checkpoint has three threads. What should your welcome say?
evals.expected_output: Briefly acknowledge that setup was found here and (if read) there are three saved threads. Offer to check agents now or change setup. Do not say 'set things up so we can pick up where you left off', show thread titles, announce version bookkeeping, or inspect the herd. Stop and wait.

evals.prompt: My saved checkpoint is on an older Shepherd version. Welcome me back without a technical changelog dump.
evals.expected_output: After lightweight checks only, state in one brief plain-language line the relevant user-visible changes, such as better accounting for multiple agents and clearer pane names. Do not say it was 'marked reviewed', foreground metadata or implementation jargon, expose checkpoint details, or start a scan. Tailor the choice to existing setup ('check agents now' or 'change setup') and wait.

evals.prompt: I choose the setup option. Help me set things up so I can pick up work next time. Once we're done, wait for me before checking agents.
evals.expected_output: Batch unanswered independent choices in a native multi-field questionnaire when supported or one compact message: scope, remembering work, clickable agent names, and Git everything local by default versus share instructions only. Use cwd and known answers as defaults; follow up only for dependent ambiguity. Confirm effects before writes and apply the Git privacy gate. Setup is not permission to inventory/read agents or search history. Finish with an offer to check agents and wait; do not automatically generate a brief.

evals.prompt: Be my Shepherd and check on my agents now.
evals.expected_output: Recognize the explicit inspection request and skip the welcome menu. Inspect this herd and return a concise numbered brief with subject-level Context, Status, Needs, Next. Missing optional setup does not block the brief; offer setup once after it without silent installation.

evals.prompt: Yes, set this directory up. I don't want a turn for every question. Use a questionnaire if you can, and ask me everything independent together.
evals.expected_output: Use one harness-supported multi-field questionnaire or a single compact message with only unanswered independent scope, remember-work, click-to-jump and Git-sharing choices. Default directory to discovered cwd; keep everything local as the Git default. Explain privacy effects plainly, obtain confirmation before writes, do not treat silence as consent, and do not inspect all agents to populate the questions. Ask follow-ups only when dependent answers need clarification.

evals.prompt: Keep my Shepherd setup local in this nested project directory. Do not change the shared .gitignore or commit anything.
evals.expected_output: Resolve the repo prefix and Git info/exclude path rather than assuming .git is a directory. Check indexed paths first; any tracked Shepherd file blocks local mode before sensitive writes. With confirmation, append preserved local-only rules anchored to the nested project and verify each planned/runtime path is ignored. Do not stage, commit, push, force-add, automatically untrack, or claim ignores remove old history. Outside Git, explain no ignore guarantee and do not init a repository.

evals.prompt: Share only Shepherd's instructions in Git; keep remembered work private. If a runtime file is already tracked or the shared ignore rules conflict, don't silently fix it.
evals.expected_output: Review instructions for sensitive content; sharing means eligible for later tracking, not automatic staging/commit/push. Any tracked runtime path blocks sensitive writes. Apply only approved local excludes allowing the exact instructions file while ignoring every other Shepherd child, including unknown runtime files, locks and temp files. Verify per-path results; a winning shared rule that defeats the requested mode blocks writes and is surfaced without automatic untracking or shared .gitignore changes.

evals.prompt: Review my herd. The skills workspace has two agents in different panes sharing the same directory: one awaits a design choice, and the other reports a finished release. Make sure neither disappears from the brief.
evals.expected_output: Preserve both recognized pane IDs, inspect enough evidence per owner rather than collapsing by workspace/cwd, and list the design decision as actionable while explicitly naming the settled release owner in Also checked. If both need action, list them independently or explicitly name both owners of one shared thread. Report unread targets as unreviewed, not settled. No permanent roster or extra discovery on bare activation.

evals.prompt: In this requested brief, one pane has the custom label Parser review, another has no meaningful label but a displayed title, a third has only its ID, and two panes share the same name. Show clickable labels without changing where the links go.
evals.expected_output: Prefer the meaningful pane label, then meaningful terminal_title_stripped, then exact ID; ignore generic harness-kind/default ID-plus-kind labels. Escape unsafe label characters and disambiguate duplicate names with pane IDs. Use URLs generated for exact verified live pane IDs; labels never become command targets or evidence of task state. Use plain labels/focus fallback when registration is absent, without inventing links.
